extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Starting from FLoRes-101 dataset sentences, three recordings were collected per sentence by three different native speakers with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70%. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponds to the input sentence, and invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes-101 dataset containing 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia, translated into 101 languages by human translators. The dev and devtest sets (2009 sentences total) were used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Native speakers recorded sentences; additional workers evaluated each recording to assess whether it corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded. Sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% was imposed when possible. Three recordings per sentence were collected from three different native speakers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: About 21.5% of sentences were missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated, indicating a validation/quality control process was applied.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings per sentence by three different native speakers; each recording also evaluated by additional workers
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers of each language, with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% imposed when possible
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to catalyze research in few-shot understanding in many languages, enabling progress towards building speech technologies for everyone, particularly for low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS is suited for several downstream tasks including ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition), Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech Language Identification, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval. It is also used for evaluating data-efficient multilingual pre-trained representations of speech.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available via TensorFlow Datasets (TFDS) and Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sentences split into train, dev, and test splits (1509, 150, 350); three recordings per sentence by different native speakers with sex ratio balance of at least 30/70%; invalid recordings discarded
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: NFC and FST normalization applied to each sentence, lower-casing, punctuation normalization and removal, splitting words into characters with '|' as word boundary token; three versions provided: raw transcript (SRC_RAW), preprocessed (SRC_NORM), and character-based (SRC_CHAR)
